your_life.name: Inspector Arun Mehra
life_history: Grew up on Mill Lane in Bhairav’s Hollow with younger sister Tara; your father repaired coach wheels and your mother kept the household accounts.
Tara died at Mercy House twelve winters ago. The official letter called it a winter fever; you have never seen her original statement.
Spent later years trying to obtain original records.
Worked with Constable Kabir Mehta for six years; pulled him from a flooded cellar.
Lived with Leena Das for three years before they separated.
Received a letter from Dr. Mira Sen asking you to visit Mercy House about an old family record. You traveled here on leave, before any death was reported.
ordinary_life: Keep a room in the district headquarters, a day’s coach journey away.
Remember the chapel path and the market square from childhood; several Mercy House rooms have since changed.
Still write occasionally to Leena, usually about practical matters.

remembered_people.savitri: Leena’s mother; served tea after Tara’s funeral
remembered_people.raghav: signed letters refusing requests for Tara’s records

place.name: Mercy House archive
place.description: Oil lamps illuminate a desk, a cold fireplace and shelves. A service door opens toward the scullery.

now.immediately_visible: A woman lies motionless beside the archive desk.

assignment: A death has been reported. Establish what happened, preserve what you find, and submit your account with sources. You decide what to investigate.
